instruction: Browse the list of women's Adidas t-shirts under $30.

metadata.explanation: Task variation: Browse women's Adidas t-shirts under $30. Same pattern as original task (filter-based shopping on NBA.com), different filter criteria. Evaluator checks filter elements and URL contain the expected filters.
metadata.verification: Reuses existing check_direct_json_object metric and active_tab_html_parse getter with class&url category.

llm_judge_reasons: URL encoding mismatch: The evaluator expects 'under $30' to appear literally in the URL, but URLs encode spaces and special characters (e.g., 'under%20%2430' or 'under+$30'). The getter's simple substring check at chrome.py:2000 will fail to match URL-encoded versions.
The term 'under $30' contains both a space and dollar sign which are typically percent-encoded in URLs, causing the url_include_expected check to likely fail even when filters are correctly applied.
Case-insensitive matching is used for HTML elements (chrome.py:1884), which is good, but the URL check may still fail due to encoding differences.
The evaluator uses dual verification (HTML elements + URL), which means if either check fails, the entire evaluation fails. The URL encoding issue makes this highly likely to produce false negatives.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Modify the URL checking logic in get_active_tab_html_parse to handle URL encoding: decode the page URL before checking, or encode the expected values before comparison.
Alternative: Remove the url_include_expected check for filters with special characters (spaces, $, etc.) and rely only on the HTML element check via class_multiObject.
Alternative: Use URL parsing to extract query parameters and check filter values from structured URL components rather than substring matching.
Test with actual NBA.com URLs to verify the class name 'filter-selector-link' exists and contains the expected filter text.
